title: Speed ramp
aka: time remapping, optical-flow slow motion

title: Datamosh
aka: I-frame removal, compression glitch, P-frame bloom
tool: FFmpeg (MPEG-4 Part 2) + Python byte editing
notice: The keyframe of the second shot is deleted, so its motion smears the pixels of the first shot. Then one frame of motion is repeated 45 times for a melting bloom, until the picture rebuilds.
use: music videos, experimental edits, glitch art
prompt: Datamosh the cut between clip A and clip B: re-encode as MPEG-4 Part 2 with no B-frames and one keyframe each, delete clip B's I-frame so its motion smears A, repeat one P-frame about 40 times for a bloom, export H.264.

title: Beat-synced auto edit
aka: cut to the beat, onset detection, music-driven edit
tool: Python (NumPy synth, STFT spectral flux) + Pillow, FFmpeg encode and AAC mux
notice: A synthesized 120 BPM track plays while the edit jumps between 21 shots. Every cut lands on a hit the script found by listening: kicks are beats, beats with a ringing crash are downbeats (white flash and a big zoom punch), and a snare fill cuts fast at the end. The strip at the bottom shows the onset curve and each detected hit.
use: music videos, social reels, trailers, auto-edited recaps
prompt: Make a 9 s beat-synced montage with sound: synthesize a 120 BPM drum-and-bass loop in NumPy (kick each beat, claps, hats, crash every bar, snare fill at the end), then detect the hits from the audio only (STFT spectral flux in low, mid and high bands; downbeat = beat with a ringing crash), cut to a new clip on every hit, white flash and 13% zoom punch on downbeats, 5% punch on beats, end card on the last hit. Show the onset curve with hit markers and a playhead at the bottom. Mux the audio as AAC.

title: Optical flow, made visible
aka: motion vectors, dense flow, Farneback, flow visualization
tool: OpenCV (calcOpticalFlowFarneback) + NumPy, fed by FFmpeg

use: VFX and tracking explainers, motion-reactive effects, data-driven particle looks
prompt: Visualize dense optical flow on my clip, 7 s 1280x720: OpenCV Farneback at half resolution between each pair of frames. Start on the footage, diagonal wipe to flow as color (HSV: hue = direction, brightness = speed, color-wheel key in the corner), cross-fade to arrows every 40 px colored by direction over the dimmed footage, then 2,400 particles advected by the flow with 12-frame glowing trails. Label each view.

title: Photomosaic zoom-out

Every tile is a moment from one of 29 clips in this catalog, picked by its 3x3 average colors, tinted toward its cell and still playing.

Start on one tile at full screen, pull back 40x eased in log space, hold, then fade the target frame in at 70%. Labels for each step.

title: Pixel sorting
aka: glitch sort, brightness threshold sort, Asendorf sort
tool: Python (NumPy argsort per row and column) fed by FFmpeg
notice: First the mask appears: only pixels inside a brightness band stay lit. Then each run of those pixels is sorted from dark to bright, along rows and later down columns, so the sunset melts into streaks while the buoy stays sharp. The bar at the bottom shows the band as it sweeps.
use: music videos, album art, glitch transitions
prompt: Pixel-sort my clip, 7 s 1280x720: show the mask first (pixels with brightness between lo and 0.985 stay lit, the rest dim), then sort each run of masked pixels along rows from dark to bright while lo sweeps from 0.55 to 0.18 and back, wipe to sorting columns, then close the band so the clean frame returns. Show a brightness bar with the band and the lo value.

title: Slit-scan time displacement
aka: time warp scan, rolling-shutter look, temporal displacement
tool: Python (NumPy per-pixel frame gather) fed by FFmpeg
notice: Every pixel shows a different moment of the Three.js clip, so orbiting spheres stretch into streaks and the columns bend. A delay map, shown in the corner, decides how far back each pixel looks: by row, then by distance from the center, then as moving waves.
use: music videos, title sequences, surreal transitions
prompt: Slit-scan time displacement on my clip, 7 s 1280x720: a delay map picks the source frame per pixel (white = now, dark = up to 2 s ago). Ease in from no delay, then rows (bottom lags), cross-fade to radial (edges lag), then a moving sine pattern, ease back to zero. Blend the two nearest frames per pixel so there are no bands. Show the live delay map as an inset and a label for each map.

title: Video stabilization
aka: deshake, warp stabilizer, camera path smoothing
tool: OpenCV (Lucas-Kanade features, estimateAffinePartial2D with RANSAC, warpAffine) + NumPy
notice: Two shots get a fake handheld shake, then OpenCV removes it without being told what it was: it tracks corners from frame to frame, adds the motion up into a camera path, smooths that path and moves each frame onto it. The graph shows the shaky path in gray and the smooth one in coral; the slow camera moves of the shots stay.
use: handheld and drone footage, screen recordings, tracking prep
prompt: Stabilize my shaky clip with OpenCV and show a before/after, 9 s 1280x720: track 300 Shi-Tomasi corners frame to frame with Lucas-Kanade, fit estimateAffinePartial2D with RANSAC, accumulate x, y and roll into a camera path, smooth it with a 31-frame moving average, warp each frame by (smooth - raw), zoom 15% to hide edges. Side-by-side panels labeled SHAKY INPUT and STABILIZED, a graph of raw vs smoothed x path with a playhead.

Corner brackets that snap in, a leader line to a dark label box (name, x/y, speed in px/s, state TRACKING / OCCLUDED / REACQUIRED in green, amber, cyan), a fading motion trail, and the box flips sides near the frame edge.

notice: The small inset shows an aperture that morphs from a circle to a hexagonal iris, a square, a triangle and finally a slit grating. The big picture is the light pattern it makes far away: Airy rings, six-point and cross-shaped starbursts, and rainbow orders from the grating. Each frame is the squared magnitude of the aperture's 2D Fourier transform, scaled per wavelength, which is why the edges fringe into color.
use: lens flare and starburst design, science explainers, abstract light backdrops
prompt: Write a Fourier optics renderer from scratch in Rust (std threads only, own radix-2 FFT) and render 8 s at 1280x720 30 fps: a 512x512 aperture mask morphs (blended signed distances, eased) from a circle to a hexagon, a square, a triangle and a five-slit grating while turning slowly. Each frame, take the 2D FFT, shift it, and sample the intensity at 12 wavelengths from 420 to 680 nm, each scaled by its wavelength, summed to RGB. Log tone map, near-black background, the aperture shown as a cream inset in the lower left.

title: Wind tunnel: a wing stalls (lattice Boltzmann in Rust)
aka: CFD, lattice Boltzmann method, smoke tunnel, vortex shedding, airfoil stall
tool: Rust with the standard library only: D2Q9 lattice Boltzmann with a Smagorinsky eddy viscosity, particle streaklines
notice: Smoke lines flow past a wing at 4 degrees and stay smooth, with a small wavy wake. Then the wing pitches up to 24 degrees, the flow tears off its top surface, and big vortices roll away behind it, tinted coral or cyan by their direction of spin. The air is 360,000 lattice cells that stream and collide 23,400 times; the smoke is 54,000 particles carried by that flow.
use: engineering and science explainers, aerospace and automotive brands, data-art backdrops
prompt: Write a 2D lattice Boltzmann wind tunnel from scratch in Rust (std threads, no crates): D2Q9 BGK on an 800x450 grid with a Smagorinsky eddy viscosity, inflow at 0.1 lattice speed, a sponge before the outlet, a NACA 2412 airfoil voxelized by scanline fill with bounce-back walls. Hold the wing at 4 degrees, then ease it up to 24 degrees so it stalls and sheds vortices. Show 27 smoke streaklines (particles released at the inlet, RK2 advection) in cream over a coral and cyan vorticity tint, a coral wing and a small angle gauge, dark background, 8 s 1280x720 30 fps.

title: Newton's prism, traced in 2D
aka: 2D light transport, spectral ray tracing, dispersion, light painting of rays
tool: Rust with the standard library only: 2D spectral light tracer (Fresnel, Snell, Cauchy dispersion), anti-aliased line splatting
notice: A white beam travels in, a glass prism fans it into a rainbow on the screen, then a lens rises into the fan and folds the colors back into a white spot, like Newton's experiment. Each frame traces 600,000 rays of single wavelengths through the glass and draws every one as a faint line, so the picture is the light itself, faint reflections included.
use: science explainers, optics and photography brands, album-style visuals
prompt: Write a 2D spectral light tracer from scratch in Rust (std threads only) and render 8 s at 1280x720 30 fps: a white beam enters from the left and its front travels across the frame, an equilateral glass prism (Cauchy dispersion, exact Fresnel, reflections kept) fans it into a spectrum that paints a rainbow on a thin screen at the right, then a biconvex lens slides up into the fan and focuses it back to white on the screen. 600,000 rays per frame, one wavelength each, drawn as additive anti-aliased lines with brightness per unit length, glow from two blurs, thin cream outlines on the glass, dark background.

title: Spectral path tracer in Rust
aka: offline renderer from scratch, Monte Carlo light transport, physically based rendering
tool: Rust with the standard library only (no crates): SAH BVH, GGX metals, next event estimation with MIS, spectral dispersion, a-trous denoiser
notice: A glass prism turns in front of neon bars and splits them into rainbows, a cut gem throws colored fire, and three glowing moons streak around a gold sphere while the focus pulls from the prism to the sphere. Each pixel averages 64 random light paths, and each path that enters the glass picks one wavelength, which is where the rainbows come from. About 1,000 lines of plain Rust on 12 CPU threads; a frame took 3.5 s on average including the denoiser.
use: learning how Cycles or Arnold work, custom offline renderers, product shots with dispersion and glossy metal
prompt: Write a path tracer from scratch in Rust with no crates (std threads only) and render a 7 s 1280x720 30 fps shot: a slowly spinning flint-glass prism and a faceted gem with a wavelength-dependent index (Cauchy, one wavelength per path), a rough gold sphere and a copper torus (GGX), a glossy dark floor, neon bar lights in coral, cream and cyan, three emissive moons orbiting fast enough to motion blur, a camera arc with a thin-lens focus pull from the prism to the sphere. BVH with binned SAH, next event estimation with MIS, 64 samples per pixel, edge-avoiding a-trous denoiser guided by albedo and normals, bloom and ACES. Write PPM frames and encode with FFmpeg.

title: A word hidden in sound (spectrogram)
aka: spectrogram art, additive synthesis, STFT, Aphex Twin trick
tool: Rust with the standard library only: TrueType reader, additive synthesizer, WAV writer, FFT spectrogram
notice: Play it with sound. A chirp rises, a low drone hums, then a buzzing cluster of tones plays, and the scrolling spectrogram shows that the sound spells MOTION. The program drew the word from a font, turned every pixel row into a sine tone whose loudness follows the letters, wrote the WAV, then analyzed it with its own FFT to draw what you see.
